extracted.intended_audience: professional mathematicians and researchers in arithmetic/anabelian geometry (particularly those engaging with IUT, its critics, and formalization efforts)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for assessing mathematical theories, proofs, and expositions (with emphasis on IUT, anabelian geometry, and Lean-style formalization): what constitutes acceptable documentation, canonical constructions, handling of indeterminacies, and the role/limits of computer formalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of passing to a larger universe for canonical constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: “the necessity of passing to a larger universe in order to obtain a canonical construction of the object of interest ... is a very substantive issue ... by no means ‘a matter of taste’.” (applies to e.g. profinite fundamental groups and cohomology modules)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: SGA1's profinite fundamental group and derived functor/cohomology constructions; identifying the larger universe with the original universe can lead to contradiction (violation of the axiom of foundation). Treat the use of larger universes as a substantive, non-optional mathematical feature whenever canonical constructions require them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assume existence of canonical choices (basepoints, algebraic closures, resolutions)
rubrics_metrics.description: “the nonexistence of a canonical choice of basepoint ... corresponds to the nonexistence of a canonical choice of algebraic closure of a perfect field” and similarly “nonexistence of a canonical choice of (injective/projective) resolution for a module.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assuming functorially canonical choices often leads to contradictions; proofs and constructions must either work without such canonical choices or explicitly account for the resulting indeterminacies (e.g., inner automorphisms, homotopy equivalences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and factor out indeterminacies (inner automorphisms, homotopy equivalences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indeterminacies arising from non-canonical choices (inner automorphism indeterminacies in étale fundamental groups; homotopy equivalences of resolutions in derived functors) are substantive phenomena that must be acknowledged and handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete handling: pass to appropriate invariants (e.g., cohomology modules) or work with canonical factorizations; do not attempt to erase indeterminacies by illicit identifications of universes or canonical choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sacrificing canonicality to avoid universes preserves substantive inter-universality
rubrics_metrics.description: “by sacrificing canonicality, one can avoid the use of universes by working with small categories, but again the unavoidable substantive aspect ... lies in the 'inter-universality' ... which manifests ... in the various indeterminacies that occur.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working in a fixed small model of ZFC or with small collections removes some set-theoretic machinery but does not remove the mathematical content of indeterminacies; be explicit about the trade-off (loss of canonicality vs. avoidance of universe apparatus).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime-strips/theta-links and other IUT constructs do not inherently trigger set-theoretic paradoxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuttal of the claim that objects like prime-strips and theta-links 'trigger set-theoretic paradoxes' (FA3): these constructs are incompatible with additive ring structure and instead require non-ring-theoretic structures (multiplicative monoids, Galois groups as topological groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate philosophical metaphors (e.g., '∈-loops') with literal set-theoretic paradoxes. Demonstrate compatibility/incompatibility with classical structures (e.g., show why additive ring structure cannot be imposed) and provide classical analogues (modular curves of genus 1; coupling of real dimensions in complex analysis) to illustrate the phenomenon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid artificially separating anabelian content from diophantine/abc aspects when they are logically intertwined
rubrics_metrics.description: “the mathematics that gives rise to a proof of the abc inequality in IUT is precisely the same mathematics as the mathematics that involves the multiradial representation and absolute anabelian geometry ...” — separation is mathematically meaningless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing claims that attempt to isolate anabelian parts from abc-related parts, require demonstration of logical independence; if the same constructions and dependencies occur across aspects, treat them as part of a single mathematical package rather than separable items for independent validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit written documentation of precise statements and complete proofs is obligatory
rubrics_metrics.description: “explicit written documentation of precise statements and complete proofs of mathematical assertions ... is the common goal of all professional mathematicians.” (CmGl) and the related demand in Fth1/Fth2 that belief in others' claims be grounded in explicit references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept reputation, hearsay, or 'faith' as substitutes for written proofs. When encountering claims of verification or refutation, ask for precise references to published materials or explicit written statements/proofs; if none exist, withhold unconditional acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demand precise references/proofs before granting belief in others' claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Queries Fth1/Fth2: require a precise reference to an explicit written documentation of a precise statement/complete proof or else avoid granting unconditional privileged status to assertions based on authority alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical test: ask whether a complete proof exists in explicit written form (preferably in a peer-reviewed journal); if not, ask whether the claimant expects unconditional deference (the 'divine right of kings' question). Use this as a standard for professional accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lean-style computer formalization as a central tool for accountability and preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Asp1/Asp2: Lean formalization provides a permanent explicit record of logical structure independent of humans and an 'ideal universal colleague' to direct writing/exposition toward; considered the best available technology for 'liberating mathematical truth from the yoke of social/political dynamics.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value and pursue Lean formalization for long-term preservation, reproducibility, and clarity. Use it to record proofs, clarify dependencies, and produce unambiguous logical artifacts; expect it to aid exposition and later automated exposition (with AI), even if it won't instantly settle social controversies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize the limits of formalization for resolving social/political disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Phenomena (LnGp, TecGp, PyGp): there can be a gap between what a formal proof verifies and human interpretation or belief; Lean formalization is not a 'magical cure' for faith-driven denial or strong social/political dynamics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using formalization, be explicit about what it achieves (permanent logical record, rigorous verification) and what it doesn't (immediate persuasion of those acting from ideology). Avoid overstating its capacity to change minds in the short term; emphasize long-term institutional and archival benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use formalization + AI as a future route to broaden access and exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Combining Lean-style formalization with AI may make it possible to automatically generate expository textbooks, video talks, or interactive dialogue tools from Lean code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage formalization projects with an eye toward downstream tooling (automated expositions, Q&A systems) that can make deep, formalized mathematics accessible to broader audiences while preserving logical precision.
